A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoVieS work and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices. Content can be matched across the substantial reformatting and supplementary-material renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original novel-view-synthesis and 3D-point-tracking results, quantitative ablations in Tables 4–6, and qualitative reconstruction, flow, and segmentation results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a quantitative VGGT-initialization comparison and qualitative DAVIS view-synthesis results.

M1.justification: Both retain dynamic splatter pixels, the VGGT-based backbone, depth and splatter heads, a time-conditioned motion head, and depth/rendering/motion objectives. Added loss specifications and initialization details document the existing approach; the scratch-initialized configuration is an ablation, not a replacement method.

E1.justification: v2 adds qualitative novel view synthesis on in-the-wild DAVIS videos with estimated camera poses (Section 4.2.2 and Figure S.1). The eight training datasets and existing quantitative benchmarks remain unchanged. Changing Table 1's caption from nine datasets to eight corrects the description of the same eight rows.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain DepthSplat, GS-LRM, Splatter-a-Video, Shape-of-Motion, and MoSca in Table 2, and BootsTAPIR, CoTracker3, and SpatialTracker in Table 3. STORM is newly discussed but not evaluated; the new initialization comparison is an ablation.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 224×224 initialization comparison with two- and six-day training budgets and DAVIS evaluation using MegaSaM poses. Appendix A.2 revises final-stage sampling from the previously described 13-frame, 518×518 setting to 2–13 frames and aspect ratios 0.5–2, although A.3 retains the fixed-setting wording. A.1 also adds Depth Pro to preprocessing. These reported changes do not establish that retained benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds an experiment testing dependence on VGGT initialization. Section 4.2.2 and Figure S.1 add qualitative robustness evidence on DAVIS with estimated poses. Existing camera-conditioning, motion-supervision, and joint-training ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run or seed counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added initialization results also lack uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports 17.97 dB DyCheck mPSNR after two days with VGGT initialization versus 16.64 dB after six days from scratch, and quantifies static-scene motion as below 1e-3. Figure S.1 replaces v1 Figure 6's reconstruction examples with new DAVIS results. Tables 2–6 retain their results; multiplying SSIM values by 100 is a reporting-scale change, not improved performance.

T1.justification: New Equations 3–4 formally specify the previously prose-described depth and rendering objectives, including an L1 gradient penalty and weighted LPIPS term. The unsquared L2 notation leaves an inconsistency with the retained MSE description. Existing deformation and motion-loss mathematics remain unchanged, with no added theorem or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim one-second joint appearance, geometry, and motion modeling, competitive multi-task performance, and zero-shot flow and segmentation applications. Although the contribution list changes 'first' to 'novel', the abstract retains the same first-time joint-modeling claim.

C2.justification: v2 newly argues that VGGT initialization only accelerates training and is unnecessary for comparable outcomes, although the reported scratch run remains worse and unconverged. The scalability limitation changes from handling large-scale scenes to handling long videos; reconstruction-quality and external-camera-estimation limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 discloses loss weights, full fine-tuning, zero-initialized camera/time embeddings, a 10% holdout when official test splits are unavailable, and 65-frame DyCheck clips. It also explains visualization normalization and dataset provenance more precisely. Conversely, v1's explicit restriction of Gaussian-attribute deformation to scale and rotation is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds STORM and DAVIS citations and removes several static-reconstruction references, including MoGe, Fast3R, and MASt3R-SLAM. Related work newly distinguishes STORM's multi-view outdoor-driving setting and drops the detailed DynaDUSt3R discussion. The main positioning relative to BTimer and NutWorld remains.

P1.justification: v2 tightens prose, merges the dynamic-reconstruction and dynamic-view-synthesis related-work subsections, reorganizes the appendix discussion, licensing, and visualization sections, and adds Tao Hu to the author list. The main introduction–method–experiments–conclusion narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: The paper and textual appendices change from single-column to two-column layout. Figures 1–2 are substantially redrawn, tables and figures are relocated, and Table 1 is shortened while its full information is retained in Table S.1. The former reconstruction panel is replaced by a four-column DAVIS visualization, and supplementary captions are expanded.

improvement.justification: Explicit loss weights, initialization and sampling details, and clearer visualization provenance improve reproducibility and interpretation. DAVIS examples and the initialization experiment provide useful additional evidence without changing the central benchmark findings. These gains are limited by the unsupported claim of comparable scratch-training outcomes and inconsistencies in the new loss notation and final-stage training description. Overall, the added transparency and evidence provide a modest quality improvement.
